subject.title: fix(google-vertex): add Google Vertex AI onboarding wizard, fix ADC auth, add provider docs

question: Should OpenClaw accept google-vertex ADC setup as a permissive onboarding contract that treats project or credential evidence as configured and lets GoogleAuth fail at request time?
rationale: The PR is proof-supplied and the implementation is plausible, but it changes provider/auth defaults, setup-written config, marker credentials, and a core fallback routing rule that require owner intent rather than automated repair judgment.

options.title: Accept the ADC setup contract
options.body: Approve the permissive auth evidence, request-time invalid-ADC failure, global/default-model onboarding writes, and core fallback routing as the intended Google Vertex behavior.

options.title: Narrow the auth and defaults
options.body: Ask the PR to keep stricter setup detection or make metadata-server ADC explicit, and reduce default config writes to the minimum maintainers want onboarding to own.

options.title: Pause behind the Vertex cluster
options.body: Hold this PR if provider boundary, location/model strategy, or broader Vertex routing decisions should be settled through the active cluster first.

recommendation.title: Accept the ADC setup contract
recommendation.body: Approve the permissive auth evidence, request-time invalid-ADC failure, global/default-model onboarding writes, and core fallback routing as the intended Google Vertex behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged production ADC support that this onboarding/auth contract builds on.
